Video analysis: Screen_Recording_2026-10-31_012428.mp4

The carrier fools the defender: he shows a pull-back to the left, then sends the ball to the right while the defender commits the wrong way. It works, but the ball ends up very close to the defender's foot, the carrier is slow to react after the touch, and his running posture is poor.

What happens in the video
Overview: a football (soccer) skills tutorial, about 35 seconds long. Two players are on an artificial pitch: a ball carrier (navy shirt, white shorts) and a defender (black kit) pressed against his back.

0.0-13.9 s: the picture is paused while on-screen arrows explain the move. A small arrow points down at the ball, a white arrow points LEFT (about 9 s), then green arrows point RIGHT (about 10-13 s).
14.0-17.0 s: the real movement plays. The carrier sends the ball to the right; the defender steps and lunges to the left and is wrong-footed; the carrier runs after the ball.
17.0-18.0 s: both players jog/sprint away.
19-28 s: slow-motion, low-angle close-ups of the feet and the ball.
29-31 s: the same situation again from the side.
32-34 s: a real match clip (a player in red, number 23) showing the same idea.
Audio was not analysed.

Coaching points (how to show the player)

Keep the ball close

Keep the ball about one small step from your body. Then you can always touch it fast, and the defender cannot reach it.

How to show the player

  1. Put two shoes on the grass in a line. One is 30 cm from your standing foot (as long as a school ruler). The other is 50 cm away.
  2. Touch the ball so it stops between the two shoes. Do it 10 times.
  3. Now show the wrong way: let the ball roll past the far shoe. Ask, 'Could a defender reach it now?'

How to check: After every touch, the ball sits between the two shoes.

Bend your knees a little

Stand a bit lower, like you are about to sit on a tiny chair. Straight legs are slow to start and easy to knock over.

How to show the player

  1. Stand tall with straight legs, like sticks. Push off and run. Say how it feels.
  2. Now bend your knees a little, like sitting on a tiny chair. Push off and run again.
  3. Ask the player which start felt faster and steadier.

How to check: From the side you can see a small bend in the knees, and the hips are a little lower.

Use one arm to feel the defender

Keep the arm next to the defender bent like the letter L. It helps you feel where he is. Never push or grab.

How to show the player

  1. A partner stands close behind the player.
  2. The player bends one arm like an L and gently touches the partner, just to feel where he is.
  3. The partner walks around slowly. The player points to where he is, with eyes on the ball.

How to check: The arm is bent and soft. The player does not push or hold.

Start moving right after you touch the ball

Take your first step at the same moment as your touch. Do not wait and watch.

How to show the player

  1. The coach claps at the moment of the touch.
  2. On the clap, the player takes the first quick step toward the ball.
  3. Time it with a phone stopwatch. In the video it took about 1 second. Try to get under half a second.

How to check: The player is already moving while the ball is still only one step away.

Chest up when you run

Run with your chest up, tall and proud. Look at the ball and the open space, not at the grass.

How to show the player

  1. The coach stands 10 steps away and holds up some fingers.
  2. The player runs toward the coach and shouts how many fingers while running.
  3. This makes the head come up and the chest lift.

How to check: The head is up, and the arms swing bent like two letter Ls.

Cool ways to do it better

Pull the ball back, then turn away (Cruyff turn)

The defender is on your back or side and you want to turn away from him.

The moves

  1. Show a small pass or shot with your touching foot (the fake).
  2. At the last moment, drag the ball behind your standing leg with the inside of the foot.
  3. Turn your body the way the ball is going.
  4. Take your first step straight away.

How to show the player

  1. Put one cone where the defender is.
  2. Walk through the 4 steps slowly with no ball.
  3. Do it with the ball. Then let a partner walk toward you as the defender.
Roll the ball under the bottom of your foot, then spin away

The defender is tight and you need to change direction in a small space.

The moves

  1. Keep the ball on the foot furthest from the defender.
  2. Put the bottom of that foot on top of the ball and roll it back across your body.
  3. Turn on your standing foot.
  4. Push the ball away with the outside of the same foot.

How to show the player

  1. Stand still. Roll the ball back and forth under the bottom of one foot, 10 times for each foot.
  2. Add the spin on the standing foot.
  3. Add a partner standing where the defender is.
One-touch pass back, then run into space

A teammate is nearby and the defender is very tight.

The moves

  1. Pass the ball back or sideways with one touch.
  2. Turn away from the defender.
  3. Run into the open space for the return pass.

How to show the player

  1. Stand with a partner 5 big steps away.
  2. Pass to the partner with one touch, then turn and run to a cone.
  3. The partner passes the ball to you at the cone.
The same move, tidier

You want to keep this exact move.

The moves

  1. Make the pull-back short and quick.
  2. Push the ball wider so it clears the defender's feet.
  3. Use two or three small touches, not one long push.
  4. Start running on the same beat as the touch.

How to show the player

  1. Make a small square with four shoes, about 2 metres wide.
  2. Do the move inside the square using 2 or 3 small touches.
  3. Count your touches. Try to need fewer big pushes and more small, quick touches.

Things I am not sure about

  • Distances and angles are estimates from a flat side-on camera, using the ball's width (about 22 cm) as a ruler. Treat them as roughly plus or minus 25%.
  • The first 14 seconds are a paused picture with arrows. The real movement is only about 14.0-17.0 s, with slow-motion replays at 19-28 s.
  • This looks like a staged demonstration: the defender may not be trying fully.
  • Audio was not analysed.
  • These findings were made by Claude from frames of the video, not by the Muse Spark model.
  • Body angles come from a pose model that follows one person per frame. Here it followed the carrier in the paused section (0-14 s) and mostly the defender afterwards, so numbers are shown only where the skeleton is on the right player.
  • Numbers marked UNSTABLE changed a lot between frames, so do not rely on them. Elbow angles were the least stable.
  • Equipment brands are named only where a logo is readable in the zoomed crops. Boots and the ball brand cannot be determined from this video.
